test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 26 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: How much time will a train of length 200 m, moving at a speed of 72 km/h take to cross another train of length 300 m completely, moving at 36 km/h in the same direction?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Relative Speed** in same direction = Difference of speeds = 72 − 36 = 36 km/h.

Convert speed to m/s: 36 × (5/18) = 10 m/s.

**Total Distance** to cover = Sum of lengths = 200 + 300 = 500 m.

**Time** = Distance ÷ Relative Speed = 500 ÷ 10 = 50 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 50 sec.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/34d686780f75f6f2546573437c03a8e403b6fe72446addd003ec3fb51972cb9d.png] 

**Given:**

Length of first train (L₁) = 200 m

Length of second train (L₂) = 300 m

Speed of first train (S₁) = 72 km/h

Speed of second train (S₂) = 36 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Time = (L₁ + L₂) ÷ (S₁ − S₂)

Conversion: 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 72 − 36 = 36 km/h

⇒ Relative Speed in m/s = 36 × (5/18) = 10 m/s

⇒ Total distance to be covered = 200 + 300 = 500 m

⇒ Time taken = 500 ÷ 10

⇒ Time taken = 50 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 50 sec.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed is S₁ − S₂. When they move in **opposite directions**, relative speed is S₁ + S₂.

Crossing Distance

To cross each other completely, the distance covered is always the **sum of the lengths** of both trains, regardless of the direction.

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5.</p
